reply_text:
*I’d hold the merge.* Two rollout-safety issues reproduced against `main`:

*CRITICAL*

1. *Rules leak between independent flags* — `flags/registry.py:13–15`
   The mutable default `rules=[]` is shared across calls. Creating `alpha` with a pro-plan rule and `beta` with an EU rule makes *both flags accept either rule*, unintentionally expanding both audiences.
   *Recommended fix:* Default to `None` and allocate a fresh list per independent flag. Add a regression test using two calls without an explicit rules list; the current tests always supply one.

2. *Missing context fields can now enable a flag* — `flags/match.py:2`
   `matches({'cohort': 'none'}, {})` returns `True`: the missing field becomes `None`, then normalizes to `"none"`. This returned `False` before the change. An explicit null context value also matches the literal string `"none"`.
   *Recommended fix:* Distinguish missing/null values before string normalization, preserving the intended string/integer matching. Add missing-field and null-versus-string regression tests.

*Validation:* All 5 existing tests pass; neither catches these reproductions. I read the full diff and all in-repo consumers. Downstream applications aren’t present here, so their compatibility remains unverified.

No code changes made; working tree is clean.
